lines: In the orchard behind my grandfather's house there was a door that opened onto nothing.
Just a doorframe, silvered with age, standing between the third and fourth apple trees.
Children were forbidden to walk through it, which is the same as being invited.
I was eleven when I went through.
Nothing happened, and that was the first magic: the grass on the other side was exactly the same green.
It took me a week to notice that the apples on that side ripened a day earlier, and that the birds sang a half-note flatter, as if from further away.
Each day I went through, I was a little more of the other side.
By midsummer my shadow had begun to arrive a few seconds after me.
My grandfather found me in the orchard that evening, watched my shadow catch up, and sighed.
"Your grandmother did the same," he said.
She said it was only a matter of choosing which apples you wanted to taste first."
